desc: Tehri Dam is the tallest dam in India and one of the tallest in the world, standing 260.5 meters high. Located on the Bhagirathi River near Tehri in Uttarakhand, it is a multi-purpose rock and earth-fill embankment dam completed in 2006. The dam generates 1,000 MW of hydroelectricity and provides irrigation water to 270,000 hectares. Its reservoir, Tehri Lake, has a storage capacity of 4.0 km³. The project involved the relocation of the entire town of Tehri.
fact: It is the tallest dam in India at 260.5 meters · It generates 1,000 MW of hydroelectricity · Its reservoir stores 4.0 km³ of water for irrigation · The project relocated the entire town of Tehri

desc: Bhakra Nangal Dam is a concrete gravity dam on the Sutlej River in Himachal Pradesh. It is the second-tallest dam in India at 225.5 meters and one of the earliest multi-purpose river valley projects built after India's independence. Completed in 1963, the dam creates the Gobind Sagar reservoir and provides irrigation to 10 million acres of land in Punjab, Haryana, and Rajasthan. The dam generates 1,325 MW of hydroelectricity and was conceived by Sir M. Visvesvaraya.
fact: It is the second-tallest dam in India at 225.5 meters · It provides irrigation to 10 million acres across three states · It generates 1,325 MW of hydroelectricity · It was one of India's first post-independence multi-purpose river valley projects

desc: Nagarjuna Sagar Dam is the world's largest masonry dam built across the Krishna River in Telangana. Completed in 1972, the dam stands 124 meters tall and stretches 1.6 km in length. It is a multi-purpose project providing irrigation to nearly 1 million hectares and generating 815.6 MW of hydroelectricity. The dam's reservoir is one of the largest man-made lakes in the world. The dam is named after the Buddhist scholar Nagarjuna and submerged the ancient Buddhist site of Nagarjunakonda.
fact: It is the world's largest masonry dam at 124 meters tall and 1.6 km long · It provides irrigation to nearly 1 million hectares · It generates 815.6 MW of hydroelectricity · Its reservoir submerged the ancient Buddhist site of Nagarjunakonda

desc: Sardar Sarovar Dam is a gravity dam built on the Narmada River in the Narmada district of Gujarat. It is one of the largest dams in India, standing 138.7 meters tall with a length of 1,210 meters. Completed in 2017 after decades of construction and controversy, the dam is the centerpiece of the Narmada Valley Project. It provides drinking water to 9,000 villages and irrigation to 1.8 million hectares across Gujarat, Rajasthan, and Maharashtra. The dam's hydroelectric capacity is 1,450 MW.
fact: It is one of the largest dams in India at 138.7 meters tall · It provides drinking water to 9,000 villages and irrigation to 1.8 million hectares · Its hydroelectric capacity is 1,450 MW · The dam was completed in 2017 after decades of construction and legal battles

desc: Hirakud Dam is a multi-purpose dam built across the Mahanadi River in Sambalpur, Odisha. Completed in 1957, it is one of the longest earthen dams in the world, stretching 4.8 km. The dam is a major flood control structure for the Mahanadi delta and provides irrigation to 436,000 hectares. The dam creates the Hirakud Reservoir, one of the largest artificial lakes in Asia spanning 743 km². The project generates 347.5 MW of hydroelectricity.
fact: It is one of the longest earthen dams in the world at 4.8 km · Completed in 1957, it provides flood control for the Mahanadi delta · The Hirakud Reservoir is one of Asia's largest artificial lakes at 743 km² · It generates 347.5 MW of hydroelectricity

desc: Mettur Dam is a large dam built across the Kaveri River in the Salem district of Tamil Nadu. Constructed in 1934, it is one of the oldest large dams in India. The dam stands 120 feet tall and spans 1,700 meters. Its reservoir, Stanley Reservoir, is the main source of irrigation water for the fertile Kaveri Delta region, supporting over 2.5 million acres of farmland. The dam generates 240 MW of hydroelectricity and is a critical component of the Kaveri water-sharing agreements between Tamil Nadu and Karnataka.
fact: It was constructed in 1934, one of the oldest large dams in India · Its reservoir supplies water to the fertile Kaveri Delta covering 2.5 million acres · It generates 240 MW of hydroelectricity · It is critical to the Kaveri water-sharing framework between Tamil Nadu and Karnataka

desc: Krishna Raja Sagara Dam, also known as KRS Dam, is built across the Kaveri River near Mysuru in Karnataka. Designed by the legendary engineer Sir M. Visvesvaraya, the dam was completed in 1931. It stands 39 meters tall and spans 2.6 km. The dam created a large reservoir that provides drinking water to Mysuru and Bengaluru and irrigates the Mandya district. The adjacent Brindavan Gardens are a famous terraced garden and tourist attraction illuminated in the evenings.
fact: It was designed by the legendary engineer Sir M. Visvesvaraya and completed in 1931 · It provides drinking water to Mysuru and Bengaluru · The adjacent Brindavan Gardens are a major tourist attraction · It stands 39 meters tall and spans 2.6 km across the Kaveri

desc: Tungabhadra Dam is a multi-purpose dam built across the Tungabhadra River in the Vijayanagara district of Karnataka. Completed in 1953, the dam stands 49.5 meters tall and stretches 2.4 km. It provides irrigation to 350,000 hectares in Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh and generates 127.8 MW of hydroelectricity. The dam's reservoir is also used for flood control and fisheries. The dam is located near the historic Vijayanagara Empire ruins of Hampi, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
fact: It was completed in 1953 across the Tungabhadra River · It provides irrigation to 350,000 hectares in Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh · It generates 127.8 MW of hydroelectricity · It is located near the historic Hampi UNESCO site

desc: Koyna Dam is one of the largest dams in Maharashtra, built on the Koyna River in the Satara district. Completed in 1963, the dam is a rubble-concrete structure standing 103 meters tall. It is the primary structure of the Koyna Hydroelectric Project, the largest hydroelectric project in India with an installed capacity of 1,960 MW. The dam is located in the Western Ghats and its reservoir, Shivaji Sagar Lake, is a major source of hydroelectric power generation. The region is seismically active, with the 1967 Koynanagar earthquake linked to the reservoir.
fact: The Koyna Hydroelectric Project is the largest in India at 1,960 MW · The 1967 Koynanagar earthquake was linked to the reservoir infilling · It stands 103 meters tall on the Koyna River · The reservoir is called Shivaji Sagar Lake

desc: Indira Sagar Dam is a multipurpose project built on the Narmada River in the Khandwa district of Madhya Pradesh. It is the largest reservoir in India by volume, with a gross storage capacity of 12.2 km³. Completed in 2004, the dam stands 92 meters tall and spans 653 meters. The project generates 1,000 MW of hydroelectricity and provides irrigation to 270,000 hectares. It is the first of the Narmada Valley mega-dams to be completed.
fact: It creates the largest reservoir in India by volume at 12.2 km³ · Completed in 2004, it was the first Narmada Valley mega-dam · It generates 1,000 MW of hydroelectricity · It stands 92 meters tall and spans 653 meters

desc: Srisailam Dam is a large hydroelectric and irrigation dam built across the Krishna River in the Nallamala Hills of Telangana. Constructed between 1960 and 1981, the dam stands 145 meters tall and spans 512 meters. It generates 1,670 MW of hydroelectricity, making it one of the largest hydroelectric projects in India. The dam's reservoir extends into the Nagarjuna Sagar-Srisailam Tiger Reserve. The ancient Srisailam Mallikarjuna Jyotirlinga temple is located nearby on the riverbank.
fact: It generates 1,670 MW, one of the largest hydroelectric projects in India · It stands 145 meters tall across the Krishna River · The reservoir extends into the Nagarjuna Sagar-Srisailam Tiger Reserve · The ancient Srisailam Jyotirlinga temple is nearby

desc: Idukki Dam is a double-curvature arch dam built across the Periyar River in the Idukki district of Kerala. It is one of the highest arch dams in Asia, standing 168.9 meters tall. Completed in 1973, the dam is part of the Idukki Hydroelectric Project, which generates 780 MW of electricity. The dam is built between two granite hills, Kuravan and Kurathi, and is a major engineering landmark. The reservoir waters flow through underground tunnels to power stations downstream.
fact: It is one of the highest arch dams in Asia at 168.9 meters · It is a double-curvature arch dam built between two granite hills · Completed in 1973, it generates 780 MW of electricity · Water flows through underground tunnels to power stations downstream

desc: Mullaperiyar Dam is a masonry gravity dam built across the Periyar River in the Idukki district of Kerala. Constructed between 1887 and 1895 by the British colonial government, it is one of the oldest dams in India. The dam stands 53.6 meters tall and is a subject of long-running water-sharing disputes between Kerala and Tamil Nadu. The dam diverts water eastward to Tamil Nadu's Theni district for irrigation. Its age and structural safety concerns have made it one of India's most controversial dams.
fact: It was constructed between 1887 and 1895, one of the oldest dams in India · It is a subject of long-running water-sharing disputes between Kerala and Tamil Nadu · It diverts water eastward to Tamil Nadu for irrigation · Its structural safety concerns have made it highly controversial

desc: Almatti Dam is a large dam built across the Krishna River in the Bijapur district of Karnataka. Completed in 2005, the dam stands 49.5 meters tall and forms the Almatti Reservoir. The dam is a key component of the Upper Krishna Project, providing irrigation to 400,000 hectares in Karnataka. Its hydroelectric plant generates 290 MW. The dam's height has been a source of interstate water disputes with Maharashtra and Andhra Pradesh due to concerns over downstream water availability.
fact: It is a key component of the Upper Krishna Project irrigating 400,000 hectares · Its height has been a source of interstate water disputes · It generates 290 MW of hydroelectricity · The dam was completed in 2005
